answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A cedar delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A sonnet check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A bridge penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 8701 identities need 8701 bonds of 44 tokens, 21338 dollars of hardware and 25 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
